title: I am the resurrection (John 11:1–27)
hookLine: Martha meets him on the road and makes her confession
carry: though he were dead, yet shall he live

cards: A message arrives across the Jordan from two sisters in Bethany, a village just outside Jerusalem. It's short, and it doesn't ask for anything directly: "Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick." Their brother Lazarus.
John adds, so we can't miss it: "Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus." And then the strangest sentence.
Right after telling us he loved them, John says that when Jesus heard Lazarus was sick, he stayed where he was two more days. John doesn't explain the wait. Not yet.

teach.h: THOMAS: LET US DIE WITH HIM.
teach.b: When Jesus finally says, let's go back to Judea, the disciples are alarmed: they tried to stone you there.
Thomas, the one later remembered for doubting, says something brave and bleak: "Let us also go, that we may die with him."
By the time they reach Bethany, Lazarus has been in the tomb four days, and friends have come from Jerusalem to comfort the sisters. Martha, hearing Jesus is near, doesn't wait at home.
She goes out to meet him on the road.
Her first words are honest, almost an accusation: "Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died." Then, in the same breath, she says she knows God will give him whatever he asks.
Jesus says: your brother will rise again. Martha answers with a hope she already holds: "I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day."
Someday. Far off. And Jesus brings it into the present tense: "I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live."
Not, there will be a resurrection. I am. Then he asks her: believest thou this?
And Martha makes her confession: "Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world."

teach.h: I AM THE RESURRECTION, AND THE LIFE.
teach.b: In Matthew's Gospel, it's Peter who says something like this. In John, it's Martha, grieving on a road, her brother four days in the tomb.

how: Jesus's words to Martha are often read at Christian funerals; in the Book of Common Prayer burial service, they are the first words said as the body is brought to the church.

games.q: you're Martha. your brother has been dead four days, and the friend who could have helped has finally arrived. what do you do?
o: stay home and refuse to see him.
go out on the road and tell him the truth.
games.why: she goes out to meet him: "Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died." then she confesses her faith.

practice: Martha said two things in one breath: if you had been here, and I believe; grief and faith together.
Find one sentence that's true for you today, about God, or something simpler: that love matters, that people can change, that the person you lost still matters, and quietly say it out loud.
If you pray, say it to God, the way Martha did; if not, say it to the room.
